mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the always-audit fact lets the model invent an authenticated RecordsLookup with no corresponding AuditEntry, which is exactly the FR-008/SC-001 violation the assertion is meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some o: Operation | o.kind = RecordsLookup and o.authenticated = BTrue and (no a: AuditEntry | a.op = o) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the care-team gate allows a Permitted RecordsLookup with no underlying active CareTeamMembership, i.e., a clinician accessing a record for a patient they are not on the care team of (FR-006, SC-010).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some o: Operation | o.kind = RecordsLookup and o.outcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.clinician = o.caller and m.patient = o.targetPatient and m.membershipActive = BTrue) }

mutation_targets.rationale: With least-privilege cleared, an AuditOfficer (who is denied RecordsLookup by the permission matrix) can produce a Permitted outcome, directly violating the per-role/per-endpoint authorisation matrix in contracts/http-api.md.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some o: Operation | o.outcome = Permitted and o.caller.role = AuditOfficer and o.kind = RecordsLookup }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the snapshot-correctness fact lets an AuditEntry record a clinician identity that does not match the actual caller of the operation it claims to describe -- the canonical misattribution failure under FR-009.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some a: AuditEntry | a.loggedClinician != a.op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the response-shape rules lets a Denied outcome ship a SummaryResponse on the wire, which is exactly the information-leak (denied vs. not-found distinguishable) that FR-007 / SC-003 forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some o: Operation | o.outcome = Denied and o.response = SummaryResponse }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the at-most-one-audit-per-operation rule lets the model materialise two AuditEntry rows for the same Operation -- the structural shape of an UPDATE that has been split into an old + amended row, which FR-010 / SC-006 forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj a1, a2: AuditEntry | a1.op = a2.op }

mutation_targets.rationale: With the auth-boundary fact removed, an unauthenticated operation can return a SummaryResponse -- a direct FR-001 / SC-004 violation (patient data observed without authentication).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some o: Operation | o.authenticated = BFalse and o.response = SummaryResponse }
